overview: Memeware's InvMove keeps the movement keys live while a GUI screen is open. On every UpdateEvent, and only when the current screen is not GuiChat, the module writes the raw keyboard state straight into the pressed flags of the forward, right, left, back and jump keybindings. MovementInputFromOptions reads those flags, so the player entity keeps producing forward, strafe and jump input while an inventory or other container screen has focus, and the C03 position stream keeps advancing under an open window.

sections.p: The module never touches packet code. It writes KeyBinding.pressed from Keyboard.isKeyDown(keyCode) for the five movement bindings, bypassing the GUI input path entirely. The GuiChat exclusion means typing in chat does not walk the player, and the handler runs on the pre update event, so the re-asserted flags are in place before MovementInputFromOptions.updatePlayerMoveState() reads them the same tick. The player controller then behaves as if no screen were open.

EntityPlayerSP.func_175161_p fires the pre UpdateEvent and sends one C03 variant per tick based on position and look deltas. With the module, position deltas stay nonzero while the inventory is open, so the server receives position-changing C06 packets (and the sprint-state C0B changes that accompany them) for a player whose server-side container is still open. Vanilla clients freeze in place under a screen, which is exactly the gap the module exploits and the fingerprint the inventory-move checks key on.

The server tracks the open window from the player's window interactions, so a position change with a live container is a contradiction it can validate. CheaterDeleter flags position-changing moves while a screen handler is open, Photon flags any movement past the breaking-time leniency and any jump, Negativity scores distance and sprint and sneak deltas from Bukkit events, and Hawk flags rotation, sprint or sneak while an inventory is open. All four are C03-corpus checks.

files.label: InvMove.java
files.explanation:
The module is self-contained: one handler consumer, one GuiChat guard, and a loop over the five movement keybindings. For each binding it assigns keyBinding.pressed = Keyboard.isKeyDown(keyBinding.getKeyCode()), which is exactly the state the vanilla input classes read (MovementInputFromOptions calls getIsKeyPressed()). Because the write happens on the pre update event, the forced state survives until the next event, and because the raw keyboard poll bypasses the screen, no GUI focus check can clear it.

The jump binding is included, so the module also permits jumping while an inventory is open, which Photon's inventory-move check treats as a separate and heavier violation. The GuiChat guard is the only behavioral carve-out, and it exists so chat text entry does not drive the player.

countering.label: InventoryMoveCheck (position change under a screen handler)
countering.explanation:
CheaterDeleter's check runs on every serverbound move through PlayerMovementListener.onMovement and keys on the exact module signature: packet.isChangePosition() while player.getCurrentScreenHandler() != null (lines 41-48). After a 500ms grace from the moment the screen opened (lines 58-59), invalidateMove flags when a horizontal delta grows while the server-side velocity on that axis is zero (lines 62-77), i.e. an accelerating walk with no applied velocity, which is precisely what forced keybind input produces. The flag is MINOR severity with a 100ms cooldown, and the data resets on window close and on damage (onPlayerDamage extends the grace by 1000ms, lines 99-104).

The module's sustained WASD movement past the grace period drives deltas that grow against zero server velocity, so the check flags on steady use. The bypass surface is real: movement that rides server-applied velocity (knockback, a moving platform) or movement confined to the first 500ms after opening does not trip it, and the check skips players near non-solid collision and in spectator. A careful module user who drifts instead of accelerates can stay under the delta-growth heuristic.

countering.label: InventoryMove (movement and jump under an open inventory)
countering.explanation:
Photon's InventoryMove listens on PlayerMoveEvent and skips everything that is not real movement: a squared distance at or below 0.005, vehicles, flight, no open inventory, damage invulnerability ticks, liquids, recent teleports or world changes, and low TPS (lines 77-100). The leniency is breakingTime (300ms base plus the speed-potion adjustment, lines 64-71) plus an optional ping leniency; a player still moving after that window with no jump-end grace and no pushing entities flags at 5 VL (lines 134-144). A jump while the inventory is open routes to handleJump at 25 VL, with one allowed jump per open and slab and bounce materials exempted (lines 147-180). The cancel action at 60 VL teleports the player back to the move origin (lines 55-62).

The module's sustained movement and its forced jump binding map directly onto both paths: walking past the 300ms breaking window flags repeatedly, and the jump keybind triggers the 25 VL jump branch unless the player stands on slab or bounce material. The one soft spot is the window itself: movement confined to the first 300ms after opening the inventory (or riding out a jump) is tolerated, which is how a module could preserve brief inventory movement, but the sustained walk the module is built for cannot hide inside it.

countering.label: InventoryMoveProtocol (Bukkit-event distance scoring)
countering.explanation:
Negativity's protocol is event-based: onMove requires an open inventory (p.getOpenInventory() != null), no elytra, trident, vehicle, water or nearby pistons, fall distance under 0.5 and server velocity at or below 0.1 (lines 33-34), then scores a transition to sprint or sneak as 5 points, and movement distance at or above the previous move's distance and at or above walk speed as a positive delta (lines 44-56). It flags once timeSinceOpen reaches 3 ticks and the score exceeds 2 (lines 57-63), and isBlockedInFight pauses the whole protocol during combat (lines 99-102).

The module produces exactly the scored inputs: sustained movement at walk speed keeps distance at or above the previous move, and holding W re-enables sprinting, which the transition check counts as 5. A flag fires from the third tick of an open inventory. The exclusions matter: water, pistons, vehicles, fall damage over 0.5 and knockback velocity all silence the protocol, and combat pauses it, so the module is cleanest to detect on flat dry ground away from fights.

countering.label: InventoryMove (rotation or sprint or sneak while open)
countering.explanation:
Hawk's check is the broadest of the set: it flags any MoveEvent where the player is updating rotation, sprinting or sneaking while hasInventoryOpen() is nonzero and the move is not a teleport accept (line 45), with a violation threshold of 3, a 0.999 decay and a 5 second timeout, punishing with a rubberband. Because vanilla sends look updates as part of every C03, any movement while the inventory is open carries an isUpdateRot flag and trips the check immediately.

The module cannot avoid the look component: func_175161_p sends C05 or C06 variants whenever yaw or pitch changed, and the module's forced movement changes the player's facing as it turns. The check's own TODO comments concede a one-tick false positive window after opening an inventory and the lack of a teleport grace, so a module that moved only within the first tick could slip one move through, but sustained inventory movement flags on the second move and rubberbands. The rotation clause also means a derp-style head spin combined with an open inventory is caught by the same path.
